# Dockable panel scenarios

Language-neutral test inputs for `Documentation/design/2026-11-27-dockable-panels-prd.md`, sprint #149; not a production schema. Native clients implement their own state and consumers. Each case has a stable `id`, a `priority` (`core` safety/usability invariant or `target` reference experience), `given`, ordered `events` and ordered `expected` observations. All strings are semantic descriptions, not literal UI text, serialized values, or implementation APIs. A consumer must account for each ID and assert supported behavior; unsupported target features are recorded as deferred with user impact, never silently skipped or counted as passed. A useful subset may ship by human decision without completing all target cases. Platform-specific alternatives are valid when explicitly reported; core assertions apply to every enabled path.

Unless overridden, `given` starts one workspace window with navigation docked left and review docked right, both pinned; two terminal sessions and a selected review/diff are alive. Panel identities, terminal process identities/output, selected worktree and review context are unchanged by every layout-only action. No event alters Git or the shared workspace descriptor. Focus is a logical accessible target, not an operating-system key code; a native equivalent is acceptable where described. Use isolated test preferences and simulated displays for deterministic tests. Observations following each event occur in order, not just at end of case.

These cases specify examples and invariants, not native integration evidence. Test actual rehosting, live PTYs, window ownership, real disconnected displays, scaling, keyboard, Narrator/VoiceOver and packaging on each target OS separately. Record PASS, FAIL or NOT CHECKED with the target and evidence. Never turn a missing feature or unrun check into a pass.
